column1: Maker of Patterns|2018|0|0|1978|8,6,6,5,7,9,8,9,8,8|Freeman Dyson|Letters reveal scientific judgment, collaboration and the social setting of research; personal detail limits mechanism density.

The Five Ages of the Universe|1999|0|0||8,5,5,8,8,8,7,9,8,8|Fred Adams; Greg Laughlin|Stellar evolution and long-run cosmic constraints form a coherent explanatory sequence; little new practical value for a cosmologist.

Time and Chance|2000|0|0||8,5,6,8,8,9,8,9,7,8|David Z. Albert|A sustained argument about probability, statistical mechanics and the arrow of time; conceptual explanation rather than a calculation course.

Physicalism and Its Discontents|2001|0|10||7,4,5,6,7,8,4,8,6,7|Carl Gillett; Barry Loewer (editors)|Competing arguments about reduction and physicalism expose assumptions; the multi-author structure limits cumulative synthesis.
Does Santa Exist?|2014|0|10||6,4,5,5,6,7,2,6,8,7|Eric Kaplan|Uses a familiar belief puzzle to examine logic and metaphysics; entertaining cases offer less technical or strategic depth.

The Atheist’s Guide to Reality|2011|0|10||6,6,5,6,7,7,5,8,7,7|Alex Rosenberg|Connects naturalism, cognition and ethics; strong eliminativist conclusions require more caution than the framing suggests.

Mistakes Were Made (but not by me)|2007|0|0||7,5,8,7,7,8,3,8,8,7|Carol Tavris; Elliot Aronson|Cognitive dissonance and self-justification transfer to institutional error correction; psychological findings vary in evidential strength.

Trespassing on Einstein’s Lawn|2014|0|0||7,5,5,7,7,7,7,6,8,7|Amanda Gefter|Explores foundational physics through interviews and a personal search; disputed interpretations and memoir reduce authority and density.
Spooky Action at a Distance|2015|0|0||7,5,5,7,7,7,8,7,8,7|George Musser|Connects nonlocality with spacetime research; frontier interpretations remain unsettled and have limited strategic application.
Cells to Civilizations|2012|0|0||8,8,8,8,8,8,6,9,8,8|Enrico Coen|Compares evolution, development, learning and culture through shared feedback and selection mechanisms; analogy is not causal proof.
Life’s Ratchet|2012|0|0||8,7,7,9,8,9,8,8,8,8|Peter M. Hoffmann|Thermal noise, molecular machinery and energy constraints explain biological organization without requiring specialist training.

The Self-Organizing Economy|1996|0|0||8,7,8,8,8,8,6,9,7,8|Paul Krugman|Spatial concentration and self-organization connect economic incentives with emergent patterns; stylized models limit empirical scope.
What Is Life? How Chemistry Becomes Biology|2012|0|0||7,7,6,8,8,8,6,8,8,7|Addy Pross|Dynamic kinetic stability offers a chemical account of life; origin-of-life inference remains partly speculative.

Creation: How Science is Reinventing Life Itself|2013|0|0||7,6,6,7,7,7,6,7,8,7|Adam Rutherford|Links origins-of-life questions with synthetic biology; some contemporary engineering examples will age faster than the mechanisms.

A Dialogue on Consciousness|2009|0|10||7,4,5,6,7,8,3,8,8,7|Torin Alter; Robert J. Howell|Philosophical dialogue tests competing theories of mind; the dialogue is an expository device rather than a fictional plot.
Touching a Nerve|2013|0|10||7,6,6,7,7,8,4,9,8,8|Patricia S. Churchland|Relates neuroscience to identity and morality; philosophical implications are less secure than the underlying biology.
Self Comes to Mind|2010|0|0||7,6,6,8,7,8,5,9,7,8|Antonio Damasio|Explains bodily regulation, feeling and the construction of self; the proposed synthesis is one contested model of consciousness.
The Problem of the Soul|2002|0|10||7,5,6,6,7,8,3,8,7,7|Owen Flanagan|Examines agency and ethical life within naturalism; conceptual distinctions matter more than technical or industrial application.

Who’s In Charge?|2011|0|10||7,6,7,7,7,8,4,9,8,7|Michael S. Gazzaniga|Connects distributed neural processes with responsibility and law; transfer depends on keeping neural evidence distinct from moral conclusions.

The Shadow of Consciousness|2015|0|10||6,5,5,6,7,7,3,6,7,7|Peter Hankins|Surveys competing explanations of experience and their unresolved problems; synthesis has greater value than evidential novelty.

Phi: A Voyage from the Brain to the Soul|2012|0|0||6,6,5,7,6,7,4,9,7,7|Giulio Tononi|Imaginary dialogues explain integrated information theory; publisher classifies it as science and philosophy. Speculative theory and ornate framing reduce confidence and density.
The Bonobo and the Atheist|2013|0|10||8,6,6,7,7,8,3,9,8,8|Frans de Waal|Primate cooperation informs moral origins; moving from observed behavior to human ethics requires explicit limits.

Good Without God|2009|0|10||6,4,5,5,6,7,1,6,7,6|Greg M. Epstein|Explains secular humanist ethics and community; philosophical advocacy alone does not establish ideological capture or partisan mobilization.
Moral Tribes|2013|0|10||7,7,7,7,7,8,4,8,8,7|Joshua Greene|Links moral psychology and intergroup coordination; normative conclusions exceed what experiments alone can establish.
A Better Life|2014|0|10||6,3,3,3,5,6,1,5,7,6|Chris Johnson|Personal accounts illustrate secular meaning and community; interview variety adds perspectives but little causal depth.
The Ethical Project|2011|0|10||8,7,7,7,7,9,3,9,7,8|Philip Kitcher|Treats ethics as an evolving social practice for resolving coordination failures; historical reconstruction is partly conjectural.

Constructivism in Practical Philosophy|2012|0|10||7,4,5,6,7,8,2,8,6,7|James Lenman; Yonatan Shemmer (editors)|Examines how practical reasons are constructed; academic arguments qualify as sustained explanation, with narrow direct domain fit.
A Significant Life|2015|0|10||7,4,5,5,7,8,1,8,8,7|Todd May|Distinguishes meaning from happiness and moral worth; useful conceptual distinctions, but limited systems and technical content.
The Call of Character|2013|0|10||6,4,5,5,6,7,1,7,7,7|Mari Ruti|Uses philosophical and psychoanalytic ideas to discuss agency and character; interpretive claims carry limited empirical support.

From Falling Bodies to Radio Waves|1984|0|0|1895|8,6,6,7,8,9,9,10,8,8|Emilio Segrè|Historical explanation connects classical discoveries with experiment and instrumentation; chronological distance incurs the separate historical deduction.

Space, Time, and Gravity|1977|0|0||8,5,5,8,8,8,7,10,8,8|Robert M. Wald|Conceptual explanation of relativity and cosmology rather than specialist calculation training; cosmological specifics reflect an older state of knowledge.
General Relativity from A to B|1978|0|0||8,4,5,8,8,9,7,9,8,8|Robert Geroch|Explains spacetime geometry through conceptual reasoning; it offers understanding without a course of tensor calculations.

Cosmology, the Science of the Universe|1981|0|0||8,6,5,8,8,7,8,9,7,8|Edward R. Harrison|Broad conceptual and historical cosmology; explanatory value survives, but modern observational developments are absent.
Origins|2015|0|0||8,8,6,8,8,8,8,8,8,8|Jim Baggott|Connects cosmic, chemical and biological development; broad synthesis is useful despite limited novelty for an expert physicist.

When Einstein Walked with Gödel|2018|0|10||8,6,6,6,8,9,7,7,9,9|Jim Holt|Essays connect mathematical ideas with intellectual history; the collection supplies varied learning but no single causal framework.

Madame Curie: A Biography|1937|0|0|1934|7,5,5,5,7,9,8,7,9,8|Eve Curie|A family biography supplies access to scientific life and persistence; affectionate selection limits critical distance. The science-biography exception applies.

Obsessive Genius|2005|0|0|1934|8,6,6,6,8,9,8,8,8,8|Barbara Goldsmith|Scientific biography relates laboratory work, institutions and personal constraints; the life story is stronger than transferable mechanism analysis.

The Born-Einstein Letters,1916-1955|1969|0|0|1955|9,5,5,6,7,9,8,10,6,8|Albert Einstein; Max Born|Primary correspondence reveals disagreements over quantum theory and scientific judgment; fragmented letters require context and earn less narrative credit.

The Comprehensible Cosmos|2006|0|0||7,6,6,7,7,8,7,8,7,7|Victor J. Stenger|Discusses physical law, symmetry and explanatory models; philosophical conclusions require scrutiny beyond the physical examples.

The Fallacy of Fine-Tuning|2011|0|10||6,6,5,6,7,7,6,8,7,6|Victor J. Stenger|Tests design arguments using physical parameters; cosmological counterfactuals and parameter independence limit certainty. No serious veto established from inspected evidence.

Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion|1779|0|10||8,4,6,6,8,10,2,10,8,9|David Hume|Philosophical dialogue tests design arguments and inference from experience; fictional speakers are an argumentative device, not a novel.

Every Thing Must Go|2007|0|10||8,7,6,7,7,8,6,9,6,8|James Ladyman; Don Ross; Don Spurrett; John Collier|Connects naturalized metaphysics with scientific structure and reduction; demanding sustained argument rather than technical skill training.

Incomplete Nature|2011|0|10||6,7,6,7,6,7,5,8,6,7|Terrence W. Deacon|Attempts to connect physical organization with purpose and mind; novel terminology and speculative transitions lower evidence and density judgments.

Faith Versus Fact|2015|0|10||7,5,5,5,7,7,3,8,8,7|Jerry A. Coyne|Compares scientific testing with faith-based belief; a critical thesis about religion is not by itself proselytizing or political mobilization.

On What Matters|2011|0|10||9,5,7,7,7,10,2,10,6,9|Derek Parfit|Detailed arguments compare moral theories and reasons for action; substantial philosophical yield, with long argumentative detours and little direct technical fit.

Not Even Wrong|2006|0|0||8,6,6,7,7,8,8,8,8,7|Peter Woit|Connects particle-physics history with testability and research incentives; criticism of string theory remains useful when separated from dated frontier claims.
Think of a Number|1990|0|0||8,5,5,7,8,9,7,8,8,8|Malcolm E. Lines|Explanatory mathematical examples connect number patterns with physical applications; modest additional utility for a specialist.
Quantum: A Guide for the Perplexed|2003|0|0||8,4,4,7,7,8,7,9,8,8|Jim Al-Khalili|Conceptual quantum explanations and paradoxes are clear; introductory level limits expert learning and strategic reuse.

Goldilocks and the Water Bears|2016|0|0||8,7,6,7,7,8,6,8,8,7|Louisa Preston|Astrobiology connects habitability, extreme organisms and planetary constraints; speculative extrapolation is distinct from observed life.

How Behavior Spreads|2018|0|0||9,8,9,9,8,9,7,9,8,8|Damon Centola|Experiments distinguish complex contagion from simple transmission; network reinforcement and coordination transfer to technology adoption and organizational change.

Beyond Weird|2018|0|0||8,5,5,8,8,9,7,8,9,8|Philip Ball|Explains quantum foundations while separating competing interpretations; useful conceptual clarity, but limited new technical content for the intended reader.
Enjoy Our Universe|2018|0|0||8,5,5,7,7,8,7,10,8,8|Álvaro De Rújula|Scientific essays connect modern physical ideas and observation; broad expert exposition rather than a technical curriculum.

The Immortalists|2007|10|0|1944|8,6,5,6,7,8,5,7,8,7|David M. Friedman|Carrel and Lindbergh's collaboration illuminates research ambition and ethical failure; the central medical and celebrity narrative triggers T11.

Totally Random|2018|0|0||8,5,5,8,7,8,7,9,8,7|Tanya Bub; Jeffrey Bub|A nonfiction graphic explanation of entanglement and information; visual examples convey mechanisms without technical proficiency training.
Making Sense of Science|2017|0|0||8,7,8,7,7,8,6,8,8,8|Cornelia Dean|Examines how evidence reaches public decisions, including uncertainty and risk; examples transfer to evaluating scientific claims.

The Edge of Physics|2010|0|0||8,7,7,8,8,8,9,8,9,8|Anil Ananthaswamy|Visits to extreme experimental sites connect physical goals with instruments, logistics and constraints; contemporary results have aged more than the engineering lessons.

Wider Than the Sky|2004|0|0||7,5,5,7,7,8,4,10,7,8|Gerald M. Edelman|Explains a biological account of consciousness and neural selection; mechanistic ideas are valuable but theoretical consensus is not established.
Mother Nature|1999|0|0||8,7,6,8,8,9,3,9,8,8|Sarah Blaffer Hrdy|Comparative evidence links maternal behavior, evolution and social constraints; broad explanatory value but low direct technical fit.

Neutrino Hunters|2013|0|0||8,7,6,7,8,8,9,9,8,8|Ray Jayawardhana|Connects particle discoveries with detector design and scientific collaboration; introductory physics limits marginal value for this reader.

The Self-Made Tapestry|1999|0|0||9,8,8,9,9,9,9,8,8,8|Philip Ball|Pattern formation connects chemistry, physics and biology through instability, feedback and constraints; rich comparative cases justify breadth.
Linked|2002|0|0||7,8,8,8,8,8,8,9,8,7|Albert-László Barabási|Network structure links technology, organizations and natural systems; broad scale-free claims need caution and do not apply uniformly.

Beyond Measure|2004|0|10||8,6,6,8,8,9,8,8,8,8|Jim Baggott|Examines quantum evidence and interpretation with historical context; philosophy is central, and the specialist reader gains distinctions more than new theory.

Dark Matter and the Dinosaurs|2015|0|0||6,7,5,6,7,7,7,10,8,7|Lisa Randall|Connects cosmology with impact history; the dark-matter extinction hypothesis is speculative, lowering evidence without equating speculation with veto.

The Music Instinct|2010|0|0||8,7,6,8,8,9,4,8,8,8|Philip Ball|Explains perception, structure and cultural variation in music; varied mechanisms provide durable learning outside the main technical priorities.

Curiosity|2012|0|0|1700|8,8,7,8,8,9,8,8,8,8|Philip Ball|Connects instruments, experiments and cultural permission for inquiry in early modern science; historical endpoint is approximate and separately deducted.

Testosterone Rex|2017|0|0||8,6,6,7,8,8,3,9,8,8|Cordelia Fine|Examines causal overreach in explanations of sex differences; methodological lessons transfer, though direct industrial and technical fit is low.
